title: Cardiac Arrhythmias in Pediatrics: Pediatric Intensive Care #1

notes.text: Recognizing pediatric rhythms
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Hemodynamic stability determines the urgency of arrhythmia management.
Sinus tachycardia often reflects an underlying cause such as fever, pain, or hypovolemia.
Supraventricular tachycardia commonly presents as a rapid regular narrow-complex rhythm, but interpretation must account for age.
Hypoxia is an important reversible contributor to bradycardia in children.

title: Pediatric Pneumonia: Latest Guidelines on Diagnosis and Treatment & a Comprehensive Explanation

notes.text: Pneumonia in children
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Pneumonia is infection of lung parenchyma and may cause fever, cough, tachypnea, and increased work of breathing.
Hypoxemia and respiratory distress are important severity findings.
Viral infection is a frequent cause in young children; not every pneumonia requires antibacterial treatment.
Age and clinical severity influence diagnostic testing, likely pathogens, and disposition.

title: Bronchiolitis: Latest Guidelines on Diagnosis and Treatment, Clinical Features and Pathophysiology

notes.text: Bronchiolitis fundamentals
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Bronchiolitis is a viral lower-airway illness affecting small airways in infants and young children.
Respiratory syncytial virus is a common cause, although other viruses also produce bronchiolitis.
Supportive care focuses on oxygenation, hydration, and feeding assessment.
Apnea can be a presenting feature in very young infants.

title: Peritonsillar Abscess (Quinsy): Pathophysiology, Clinical Features, Diagnosis and Treatment

notes.text: Peritonsillar infection
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Peritonsillar abscess is a collection of pus adjacent to the tonsil.
Trismus and a muffled voice support the diagnosis in the appropriate setting.
Uvular deviation away from the affected side may be present.
Airway compromise is a major concern and requires urgent assessment.

title: Retropharyngeal Abscess & Lateral Pharyngeal Abscess and Lemierre Disease All Explained

notes.text: Deep neck space infection
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Retropharyngeal infection may cause fever, neck stiffness, dysphagia, and airway symptoms.
Contrast-enhanced CT may help define a deep neck collection when the airway is stable and imaging is appropriate.
Lemierre syndrome involves septic thrombophlebitis of the internal jugular vein, often after oropharyngeal infection.
Fusobacterium necrophorum is a classic organism associated with Lemierre syndrome.

title: Airway Foreign Body: X Ray Examples, Clinical Features, Diagnosis and Treatment

notes.text: Foreign body aspiration
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Sudden choking followed by cough or unilateral wheeze suggests airway foreign body aspiration.
Air trapping can result from a partial ball-valve obstruction.
Normal radiography does not exclude an inhaled foreign body.
Bronchoscopy is used for definitive evaluation and removal when clinically indicated.

title: Bacterial Tracheitis: Clinical Features, Etiology, Diagnosis and Treatment

notes.text: Bacterial tracheitis
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Bacterial tracheitis can cause severe upper-airway obstruction through inflammation and thick secretions.
Staphylococcus aureus is a recognized causative organism.
Toxic appearance and high fever may help distinguish the illness from uncomplicated viral croup.
Airway management takes priority when obstruction is suspected.

title: Epiglottitis: Signs and Symptoms, Causes, Diagnosis and Treatment All Explained

notes.text: Epiglottitis recognition
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Epiglottitis is inflammation of supraglottic structures that can rapidly obstruct the airway.
Drooling and difficulty swallowing are important clinical clues.
Tripod positioning may reflect an attempt to improve airflow.
Controlled airway assessment is essential; unnecessary agitation and provocative examination may worsen obstruction.

title: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis) Explained: Pathophysiology, Signs & Symptoms, Diagnosis & Treatment

notes.text: Croup recognition
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Subglottic edema is a key mechanism in croup.
Barking cough and inspiratory stridor are characteristic clinical findings.
Parainfluenza viruses are common causes.
Stridor at rest indicates more significant obstruction than stridor only during agitation.

title: Junctional Rhythm: Pathophysiology, ECG Characteristics, Classification, Causes and Treatment

notes.text: Junctional rhythms
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
AV junction tissue can act as an escape pacemaker when sinus impulses fail or are not conducted.
Retrograde P waves may appear before, within, or after the QRS complex.
Narrow QRS complexes are common if ventricular conduction is otherwise normal.
Clinical context distinguishes a protective escape rhythm from an arrhythmia requiring treatment.
